target_pattern: Use haber in three high-frequency systems: auxiliary perfect tenses, impersonal existence forms (hay/habia/hubo/habra), and impersonal obligation with hay que + infinitive.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Treating haber as possession have and translating directly.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Haber is a structural verb for perfect tenses and impersonal existence/obligation, while tener handles possession.
target_pattern_formula: hay is fixed for singular and plural
natural_examples: Habiamos terminado antes de la reunion.
Hay muchas personas en la sala.
Hay que revisar los datos hoy.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: He comido. -> change subject to nosotros.
Base: Han escrito una carta. -> change direct object to plural cartas.
Base: Ella ha abierto la ventana. -> make it negative.
Base: Yo he puesto los papeles en el escritorio. -> change subject to usted.
Base: Has visto la pelicula? -> change to statement with yo.
Base: Hay una silla disponible. -> change noun to plural sillas.
Base: Hay mucho trafico en la ciudad. -> change to past incomplete background.
Base: Habia muchos carros en el estacionamiento. -> change to preterite event form.
Base: Hubo un concierto en el parque. -> change to future.
Base: No hay cafe. -> change to affirmative with te.
Base: Yo habia estudiado antes del examen. -> change subject to ellos.
Base: Ella habia terminado la tarea. -> make it question form.
Base: Hay que estudiar para aprender. -> change infinitive to escuchar.
Base: Hay que cortar el apio. -> make it negative recommendation.
Base: Habra un concierto el viernes. -> change weekday to sabado.

prompts: Have you eaten? (Has comido? vs Tienes comido?)
We have seen that movie. (Hemos visto esa pelicula. vs Somos visto esa pelicula.)
There are people here. (Hay personas aqui. vs Estan personas aqui.)
There was an accident. (Hubo un accidente. vs Habia un accidente as completed event)
There was a lot of noise, background. (Habia mucho ruido. vs Hubo mucho ruido in background context)
There will be a concert. (Habra un concierto. vs Tendra un concierto.)
One has to practice. (Hay que practicar. vs Es que practicar.)
They had prepared everything. (Habian preparado todo. vs Tuvieron preparado todo.)
Is there milk? (Hay leche? vs Esta leche?)
I have done the task. (He hecho la tarea. vs Tengo hecho la tarea.)

common_errors.why_it_happens: Mixing possession tener with auxiliary haber.

common_errors.mistake: Hubo mucho ruido for background context
common_errors.why_it_happens: Not distinguishing event and background frames.

common_errors.mistake: Habia un accidente for completed incident report

common_errors.why_it_happens: Trying to agree participle with noun.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Past participle stays fixed in compound tenses.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Applying regular participle to irregular verb.

common_errors.correct_spanish: Use impersonal chunk hay que + infinitive.
